description: The analyzer allows primary adapters to import ports and use cases and secondary adapters to import ports only, and a test keeps every shipped statement of rule 4 in line with that table.

specs.description: A primary adapter that imports a use case is not a boundary violation.
specs.given: A project with a file under adapters/primary/ that imports a module under usecases/
specs.when: The project is analyzed for boundary violations
specs.then: No boundary violation is reported for that import, and get_violation_rule reports adapters/primary → usecases as allowed

specs.description: A primary adapter that imports a port is allowed.
specs.given: A file under adapters/primary/ that imports a module under ports/
specs.then: No boundary violation is reported for that import

specs.description: A secondary adapter that imports a port is allowed.
specs.given: A file under adapters/secondary/ that imports a module under ports/
specs.then: No boundary violation is reported for that import

specs.description: A secondary adapter must not drive a use case.
specs.given: A file under adapters/secondary/ that imports a module under usecases/
specs.then: A boundary violation is reported for that import, and get_violation_rule reports adapters/secondary → usecases as not allowed

specs.description: A primary adapter must not import domain directly.
specs.given: A file under adapters/primary/ that imports a module under domain/
specs.then: A boundary violation is reported for that import

specs.description: A secondary adapter must not import domain directly.
specs.given: A file under adapters/secondary/ that imports a module under domain/
specs.then: A boundary violation is reported for that import

specs.description: Neither adapter kind may import the other adapter kind.
specs.given: A file under adapters/primary/ that imports from adapters/secondary/, and a file under adapters/secondary/ that imports from adapters/primary/
specs.then: A boundary violation is reported for each import

specs.description: The allowed targets for adapters are exactly these sets.
specs.given: Any import whose source layer is an adapter layer and whose target layer is any hex layer
specs.when: get_violation_rule is asked whether the import is allowed
specs.then: It is allowed only when the source is adapters/primary and the target is ports or usecases, or the source is adapters/secondary and the target is ports. Every other adapter-sourced import is refused.

specs.description: hexa still grades itself at the top grade under the table.
specs.given: The hexa repository, whose CLI commands are primary adapters that call the analysis and execution use cases
specs.then: No boundary violation is reported for CLI → usecases imports, and hexa_grades_itself_by_ratchet passes

specs.description: A newly scaffolded project's CLAUDE.md states the rule the analyzer enforces.
specs.given: A fresh directory
specs.when: hexa dev init scaffolds a project
specs.then: The generated CLAUDE.md states rule 4 as: adapters/primary/ may import ports/ and usecases/, and adapters/secondary/ imports ports/ only

specs.description: An existing project gets the corrected rule when refreshed.
specs.given: A project scaffolded before this change, whose CLAUDE.md says adapters/primary/ imports from ports/ only
specs.when: hexa refresh is run in it
specs.then: Its CLAUDE.md states that a primary adapter may import ports/ and usecases/

specs.description: No shipped document still says primary adapters import ports only.
specs.given: The claude-md-hexa-section.md template, CLAUDE.md, README.md and ARCHITECTURE.md
specs.when: Each is searched for its statement of rule 4
specs.then: None of them says adapters/primary/, or adapters in general, import ports/ only

specs.description: The superseded ADR stays as it was written.
specs.given: ADR-2609121400, which states that adapters import ports/ only
specs.then: ADR-2609121400's text is unchanged. ADR-2610261356 is the record that refines its rule 4.

specs.description: The docs gate passes when every document matches the table.
specs.given: The table allows primary → usecases, and all four documents say a primary adapter may import ports/ and usecases/
specs.then: The test passes

specs.description: The gate fails when a document is stricter than the table.
specs.given: The table allows primary → usecases, and the template states "4. **adapters/primary/** imports from **ports/** only."
specs.then: The test fails with a message that names the offending statement and says the analyzer allows a primary adapter importing usecases

specs.description: The gate fails when the table is stricter than the documents.
specs.given: allowed_targets is changed so that AdaptersPrimary allows only Ports, and the documents still say a primary adapter may import usecases
specs.then: The test fails because the documents state rule 4 differently from what get_violation_rule reports

specs.description: A drift in just one of the four documents is enough to fail the gate.
specs.given: Three documents state rule 4 correctly, and README.md alone says adapters import ports/ only
specs.then: The test fails and names README.md

specs.description: The gate checks the docs against the analyzer's answer, not against a fixed string.
specs.given: Any setting of whether primary → usecases is allowed, and any wording of rule 4 in the four documents
specs.then: It passes exactly when every document's rule 4 agrees with what get_violation_rule reports for primary → usecases

specs.description: A project can enforce the stricter rule with its own test.
specs.given: A project with a local test that reads src/adapters/primary/ and fails on any import of usecases/, and a primary adapter that imports a use case
specs.when: The project's own tests run and hexa grades it
specs.then: The local test fails, and hexa reports no boundary violation for that import

specs.description: hexa has no per-project setting that makes the analyzer stricter.
specs.given: A project that wants primary adapters to import ports/ only, with no local test for it
specs.when: hexa analyzes a primary adapter that imports usecases/
specs.then: No boundary violation is reported. The stricter rule is not configurable per project; that is deferred to issue #21.

specs.description: Allowed is not required: generated adapters that import ports only are not flagged.
specs.given: A generated HTTP primary adapter that imports ports/ only (ADR-2610100005)
specs.then: No violation and no warning is reported for leaving out usecases/ imports
